about: Every material error found in our work, who or what produced it, how it was found and what changed. Register rule P10. The page transparency/performance-log.html is generated from this file by build/transparency/build_performance_log.py. Never edit an entry after it is written except to close it.

functions.Manager: Plans the work, routes it and holds the rules
functions.Data and analysis: Pulls official data, benchmarks, models and forecasts
functions.Scanning: Sweeps data releases, policy changes and forward dates
functions.Policy: Interprets policy and writes the policy products
functions.Verification: Fact-checks and reproduces work before it ships
functions.Not recorded: The record at the time did not say which function produced it

types.Source or edition: Wrong source, stale edition, or a fact taken from something other than the primary source
types.Unsupported claim: A statement the data or the source does not support
types.Data handling: A figure pulled, filtered or calculated wrongly
types.Completeness: Something that should have been covered was missed
types.Code or reference: A wrong geography code, dataset id, filter or identifier
types.Process: The wrong task, or a working rule not followed

stages.Published: Reached the site or a document sent out
stages.Draft: Reached the site owner in a draft, a working document or a chat answer, and stopped there
stages.Caught by checks: Caught by our own verification before it reached the site owner

probation.reason: Repeat entries of the same kind within 90 days: Code or reference (E-2026-21, 22), Unsupported claim (E-2026-19, 23, 26, 27, 28, 32, 34, 36), Completeness (E-2026-20, 30, 31, 35), Source or edition (E-2026-24, 37). The threshold was first met on 24 October 2026 and recorded late, on 30 October 2026

entries.product: Four dashboards on this site
entries.found_by: Full verification audit of every product
entries.what: Written commentary contradicted the data embedded in the same page. An inverted Whickham house-price claim, a false 'top half' sentence on the Explore Local Statistics scorecard, a reversed vacancies clause on the Employer Skills Survey dashboard and an unsupported policy claim
entries.fix: All four corrected on 15 July 2026. A check that re-reads every sentence of commentary against the final data was added to the dashboard publishing steps

entries.product: Gateshead Business Map
entries.found_by: Full verification audit of every product
entries.what: The build script's NOMIS query for BRES left out the latest-date filter and took the first value returned, which was 2015. The map showed 98,000 employees where BRES 2024 gives 95,000
entries.fix: Script fixed at source on 28 July 2026 so it cannot recur on the monthly refresh

entries.product: Chat answer to the site owner
entries.what: An answer quoted a held scorecard figure for workplace pay (£590.10) labelled as ASHE 2025. A fresh pull the same day gave £670.30, below the North East, which reversed the point being made
entries.fix: Rule G7 written. Every figure comes from a fresh pull of the latest edition, or carries its true edition

entries.product: A document sent out
entries.what: Deprivation ranks were quoted 'of 32,844', which is the 2019 count on 2011 boundaries. The 2025 indices rank 33,755 neighbourhoods
entries.fix: Corrected on 23 July 2026 and written into the rules as D5

entries.product: Weekly What's New
entries.what: The instruction to complete outstanding actions was read as a verification report's open list rather than the production calendar. A whole session went on the wrong task and the overdue What's New was not produced that day
entries.fix: Rule G9 written. A small set of instructions now has a fixed meaning that is matched before anything is interpreted

entries.product: Weekly What's New, 3 August 2026 and later editions
entries.what: The Cabinet Statement 'Rewiring the State' of 31 July 2026 was reduced to a Budget-date item. Its non-fiscal half, on strategic authority rollout, boundary alignment, devolving by default and employment support, went unreported in every edition
entries.fix: Central government publications are now never filtered out, and every departmental feed item is listed in a complete log

entries.product: A labour market product in draft
entries.what: A draft explained wider Gateshead survey intervals by a cut to the Annual Population Survey sample boost. ONS documents a cut only to the Scottish boost
entries.fix: Removed before publication and written into rule D2

entries.product: Weekly What's New, editions to 8 September 2026
entries.found_by: Reconciliation against a fresh pull from gov.uk
entries.what: The departmental log was short by roughly half. The newsletter inbox script cut long emails partway through, so items such as MHCLG's review of local government reorganisation (7 September 2026) never reached the log. The log was checked only against the inbox, so the check kept passing
entries.fix: Truncation fixed on 8 September 2026. The gov.uk search API became the completeness check, and each edition states its counts

entries.product: Weekly What's New, 15 September 2026
entries.found_by: Count check on the first build
entries.what: A wrong organisation identifier for MHCLG returned no rows and no error, so the log had no MHCLG items and still reconciled with itself
entries.fix: Both MHCLG identifiers are now queried, and every feed must return a non-zero count before the log is built

entries.product: Local Outcomes Framework comparator dashboard
entries.found_by: Verification against the ONS geography register
entries.what: A correction on 29 July 2026 swapped the geography codes for Barnsley and Sheffield in a reference file. The dashboard carries the invalid code, so Barnsley is silently missing from two of its comparator groups
entries.fix: Reference files corrected on 18 September 2026 and rule D9 written. The dashboard itself still needs a full rebuild, which is deferred and tracked as an open defect

entries.product: Local Economic Assessment review response
entries.what: A local skills plan's sector list was taken from press coverage of a different plan rather than from the plan itself
entries.fix: Rule G7a written. Policy facts and dates are quoted from the primary document, never from a search result or press summary

entries.product: Local Economic Assessment review response
entries.what: A correctly sourced release date for UK Business Counts was changed to a wrong one on the strength of a dataset landing page, when the ONS release calendar had it confirmed
entries.fix: Rule G7a now says the release calendar is the authority on release dates

entries.product: Local economy review
entries.what: Claims about other places were not traced to source. A figure was taken from a secondary account, growth rates could not be traced, and one place was called the 'only' one with results
entries.fix: Rule P8 written. Claims about other places pass a four-point check before they are used

entries.product: Local economy review
entries.what: Four recommendations were for things that already existed, including a programme already commissioned for Gateshead and an evaluation already running to 2031
entries.fix: Rule P7 written. Existing provision is searched for before any recommendation is made

entries.product: Local economy review
entries.what: The review was commissioned to improve the AI team's analysis but was read as advice to the council's team, so its lessons were written for the wrong reader
entries.fix: Rule G10 extended. Every review or recommendations brief names whose actions it recommends and who reads it

entries.product: Monthly Policy Update, August and September 2026
entries.what: Work on the income tax base was reported as outstanding in two editions, although it had been done on 31 July 2026
entries.fix: Corrected in the October 2026 edition

entries.product: Monthly Policy Update, September 2026
entries.what: The edition said August's high streets package promised a consultation. It did not
entries.fix: Corrected in the October 2026 edition

entries.product: Weekly What's New, 2 October 2026
entries.what: The business department now publishes under a second organisation identifier. Querying the old one alone missed eight items, including the opening of the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme
entries.fix: Both identifiers are now queried

entries.product: Meanwhile use research and guidance review, draft of 23 October 2026
entries.what: The draft said the MHCLG Appraisal Guide supports a local GVA per £1 headline in place-based analysis. MHCLG 6.21 and 6.26 put output and job counts in the strategic case and value place benefits as welfare, so the proposed headline did not follow the guidance it cited. The claim also reached Nathaniel in a chat summary
entries.fix: Report rewritten: welfare-based ratios for Gateshead and the UK, with local GVA and jobs reported as indicators; the original combined figure offered only as a labelled alternative

entries.product: Meanwhile use research and guidance review, draft of 23 October 2026
entries.what: The draft proposed a UK benefit-cost ratio without saying which benefits it would count once GVA was excluded, although the working notes held the answer (value of the space to its occupier). It also omitted rejected precedents, the search method and conflicts with four agreed decisions
entries.fix: Value of the space added as an explicit decision; precedent table now shows compliance with guidance and what was rejected and why; decision table covers all fourteen changes

entries.product: Town Centre Activation Value Model, build of 23 October 2026
entries.what: In the blank workbook, inputs left empty were misread: a blank floor area unit was taken as square metres (about ten times the jobs), a blank break clause as no break clause, a blank participant group or cost grade broke the Results sheet, and a missing rateable value was not flagged. The demo file was unaffected because every input was filled in
entries.fix: Blank inputs now take the stated defaults (sq ft, break clause, cost grade 4, the first participant group); results stay blank with a prompt until the use, period and rateable value are entered; Results, Sensitivity and Compare are guarded against errors and were rechecked empty and part-filled

entries.product: Town Centre Activation Value Model, build of 23 October 2026
entries.what: The chance that the unit would have been let commercially anyway was netted off jobs and the value of the space but not off volunteering, participation, visitor spend, avoided costs or the rates transfer, which overstated the worked example's ratio (0.14 against 0.12). Council-owned units also counted empty rates the council would pay itself as a public cost with an offsetting private gain
entries.fix: The let-anyway chance is now netted off every benefit and the rates transfer, consistently in the engine, workbook and calculator; council-owned units carry no empty rates transfer and no council rent; all three implementations retested on eleven cases

entries.product: Budget 2026 and Business Rates Retention briefing for the Head of Service, sent 28 October 2026
entries.what: A key message said mayors take a 20% share of business rates in exchange for Investment Funds, Mayoral Capacity Funding and Local Growth Funds. The sources describe two separate things: a share of business rates income in exchange for those grants, and a permanent 20% share of growth (Red Book 6.42, Fiscal Devolution Roadmap 2.27, Policy Costings p28). The sentence came from our draft and three verification passes checked quotes and attribution but not whether two descriptions had been joined
entries.fix: Correct wording supplied to the site owner for any onward use. The measures register now records both wordings against their own sources, and the verification brief for products now checks for claims that merge two descriptions of one measure

entries.product: Budget 2026 list of policy decisions (product 1), draft of 28 October 2026
entries.what: Four errors in the measures register before the list was presented: the fuel duty extension dated from 1 July 2027, its end date, instead of 1 January 2027; the illegal waste sites measure dated 2027-28 instead of 2026-27; the high needs line described without the explanation in the Policy Costings; the electric vehicle charging measure missing its 100 million pounds and Spring 2027 start. The Red Book indexer had also dropped 12 paragraphs where a drop-cap letter split from its word
entries.fix: Dates and sentences corrected from the Policy Costings and Red Book, Policy Costings pages now cited, indexer fixed to rejoin split drop caps (626 paragraphs, no gaps) and coverage log re-ticked

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis and implications for Gateshead (product 2), draft of 29 October 2026
entries.what: Four errors before the draft reached the site owner: section 31 compensation quoted as 20.87 million pounds due to Gateshead when that is the total across all shares and the council share is 10.23 million pounds (NNDR1 2026-27); the national and local ranked lists were not in the order their stated methods give; and the note said no document says which share the mayoral 20% comes from, when the OBR says growth accrues to mayors rather than central government (EFO para 3.19)
entries.fix: Section 31 split by share, both lists reordered with the method and its limits stated (the Defence lines described separately because they offset), the 20% passage rewritten from the OBR and roadmap wording, and 15 further accuracy and 10 brief points applied

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, short version, draft of 29 October 2026
entries.what: A repeat of E-2026-23. An executive summary bullet opening 'The budget states' carried a claim found only in the Fiscal Devolution Roadmap (that the mayoral share will not affect councils' core funding). Cutting the gate-checked version down also dropped qualifiers: the Treasury assumption behind the 2.6% real-terms fall, the business case and legislation conditions, 'emerging proposition', and two hedges on our own inferences
entries.fix: Attribution split between the Budget and the Roadmap, qualifiers restored and 16 points applied. Any cut-down version now gets its own verification against the full version before it is presented

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, full version, and Budget 2026 summary draft
entries.what: A summary line merged two different SEND descriptions: it said councils' SEND deficits move to central funding from 2028-29. The OBR says SEND spending is centrally funded from 2028-29, and that 90% of deficits to the end of 2025-26 will be reimbursed, with no commitment after that. The full economic analysis carried the merged line in its council funding bullet while its own detail was right, and the summary draft copied it
entries.fix: Both now say spending moves to central funding from 2028-29, 90% of deficits to the end of 2025-26 are reimbursed, and there is no commitment after that. The full economic analysis was rebuilt

entries.product: Budget 2026 summary (House of Lords Library style), draft of 29 October 2026
entries.what: Two reaction quotes were narrowed. The Resolution Foundation's 'one in twenty' figure covers the North East, North West and Yorkshire and The Humber together, but was given for the North East alone. The CBI quote on business rates relief dropped 'will be welcomed but', turning a mixed verdict into a negative one
entries.fix: Both restored in full in the reaction and Gateshead sections

entries.product: Budget 2026 summary (House of Lords Library style), draft of 29 October 2026
entries.what: Six endnotes did not hold the claims they were attached to: the fiscal rule target year cited Hansard rather than OBR Table 7.1, the £14 billion debt interest figure needed OBR paragraph 5.30, the savings and property tax rates needed Budget paragraphs 6.246 and 6.247, the devolution paragraph's levy and 100% retention claims needed Budget paragraphs 4.60 and 4.66, and one sentence on borrowing costs had no endnote
entries.fix: Endnotes corrected and the missing one added. The fan charts were also re-rendered without their in-image Figure 1 and Figure 2 titles, which clashed with the page's numbering

entries.product: Budget 2026 summary (House of Lords Library style), draft of 29 October 2026
entries.what: The brief review found the political reaction left out the DUP and Plaid Cymru, the Rewiring the State Delivery Plan was missing, and technical terms (percentile, confidence interval, rateable value, multipliers, headroom, CPI, real terms, retention zones) were used without a plain-words gloss for a public page
entries.fix: DUP and Plaid Cymru quotes added from Hansard, the Delivery Plan line added, and plain-words glosses written in

entries.product: Budget 2026 measures register, OOTLAR and TIIN reconciliations of 29 October 2026
entries.what: The reconciliation covered the OOTLAR and every TIIN but not the other half of the plan's rule, every OBR-certified costing. Ten of the 17 recostings in Red Book Table 6.4 had no register entry, including the salary sacrifice cap, the Plan 2 student loan threshold freeze and inheritance tax on unused pensions. One impact note filed by the Department for Education rather than HMRC was also missed
entries.fix: Table 6.4 is now reconciled in the same script, with ten new register rows, and the Department for Education impact note is added to the documents list

entries.product: Budget 2026 measures register, OOTLAR and TIIN reconciliations of 29 October 2026
entries.what: Four new register sentences did not match their source. The Oil and Gas Revenue Levy start date was attached to the wrong event, 3.5% was given as the rise in the National Insurance Lower Earnings Limit when it was the uprating basis (the limit rises 3.1%), a 'rather than change the law' clause had no source, and two vaping duty dates were paired with the wrong powers. Five partial matches were recorded as full matches, and several TIIN costing differences were missed by the parser
entries.fix: All corrected and re-checked by verification. The parser now reads every table format, and every TIIN costing difference is recorded with its explanation, or marked unexplained where nothing published accounts for it

entries.product: Budget 2026 policy decisions list (product 1) and economic analysis draft of 29 October 2026
entries.what: Two register sentences carried Table 6.1 mechanics against the author's steer of no line numbers: one ended 'and line 41 delivers them from capital budgets' and another began 'This line scores the capital grant element'. Both were in the policy decisions list already sent, and resurfaced when the economic analysis listed all 98 decisions
entries.fix: Both sentences rewritten at source in the register script, and the policy decisions list and the analysis rebuilt from it

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, checklist revision of 29 October 2026
entries.what: The checklist revision merged separate statements: the OBR's 'more likely than not' was attached to landlords passing on tax when it belongs to rents rising as demand outstrips supply, and the British Business Bank's £6.5 billion of lending was described as part of its £5 billion of capacity. The mayor's 20% illustration had no price basis or reset assumption, the electricity VAT quarter assumed even use, and BRES sector shares were given to a decimal place from rounded cells
entries.fix: All reworded to their sources, the illustration labelled at 2026-27 prices with its assumptions, and the sector shares rounded

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, SEND and council housing revision of 30 October 2026
entries.what: The draft said we had found nothing on what happens to a SEND deficit balance when the statutory override ends. MHCLG's settlement response of February 2026 already says councils must meet any residual deficit from their own resources in 2028-29, and that further support for 2026-27 and 2027-28 will be confirmed
entries.fix: The MHCLG position added to both versions, with the approximately £0.4 million residual for Gateshead stated

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, SEND and council housing revision of 30 October 2026
entries.what: The draft said Gateshead's Housing Revenue Account had the same strain the OBR describes, when the council's paper shows it on budget with a planned use of reserves, and said the £1.5 billion for council homes applied to us directly, when holding stock shows relevance rather than access to the money
entries.fix: Reworded to what the papers show and hedged, with the limit of the evidence stated

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, SEND and council housing revision of 30 October 2026
entries.what: The draft treated Gateshead's High Needs Stability Grant as conditional on plan approval and eligibility, when DfE had published allocations the day before, including £3,413,085 for Gateshead
entries.fix: Both versions rewritten on the published allocation, confirmed in DfE's workbook

entries.product: Budget 2026 summary, additions of 30 October 2026
entries.what: The SEND sentence added to the public page drifted from the checked analysis. It stated approximately £3.5 million uncovered as fact when it rests on a July projection, left out the council's own review and its share of the deficit, and did not say the deficit is held separately until 31 March 2028
entries.fix: Reworded to the checked analysis before publication

entries.product: OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook one-page summary, October 2026
entries.what: The SEND sentence gave the OBR's annual cost of councils' SEND deficits (£3 billion to £6 billion) as if it were the stock of deficits, and set it beside Gateshead's cumulative deficit so the two read as the same path. The £3.792 million was also sourced to the July Cabinet paper rather than the September scrutiny pack
entries.fix: Restored 'the annual cost of', added the 90% reimbursement, compared Gateshead on its 2026-27 overspend and corrected the source before the summary was presented

entries.product: OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook one-page summary, October 2026
entries.what: Several 'The OBR states' sentences dropped qualifiers or carried our own reading: council building constraint without 'many' and 'significantly increase', the welfare cap breach without 'once the margin is included', real earnings flat in 2027 only (the OBR says 2027 and 2028), and inferences on council funding, SEND and housing not marked as ours
entries.fix: Reworded to the OBR's own qualifiers and marked each inference 'on our reading' before the summary was presented

entries.product: Budget 2026 Policy Decisions (Word list, the 98 decisions in the Budget analysis, and the new web list)
entries.what: Sentences said more than the sources: the Cambridge pilot described as funded by capital grant when the Budget says repayable finance, the Defence Investment Plan line inferred how the remainder is funded, the mayoral business rates share stated as settled where two of three sources make it conditional, and the medical deputies line gave no direction of change
entries.fix: Reworded from the Budget, the Policy Costings and the Fiscal Devolution Roadmap in the measures register and on the web list before publication. The Word products keep the old wording until rebuilt

entries.product: Budget 2026 Policy Decisions (Word list, the 98 decisions in the Budget analysis, and the new web list)
entries.what: Sentences dropped what a reader needed: the cash ISA line read as no change when a planned cut to £12,000 was cancelled, Your First Home omitted that it covers new-build homes in England only, the mileage line omitted that 55p was already temporary and the upper rate's rise from 25p, tax debt recovery omitted its limits, and the double taxation relief omitted that it covers individuals only
entries.fix: Added to the register and the web list before publication. The Word products keep the old wording until rebuilt

entries.product: Budget 2026 summary
entries.what: The summary said the cash ISA limit stays at £20,000 without saying a planned cut to £12,000 had been cancelled, and described Your First Home without saying it is for new-build homes
entries.fix: Both lines corrected, with a dated correction note at the top of the page

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, 3 to 4 page version, draft of 30 October 2026
entries.what: The first 3 to 4 page draft gave Gateshead's SEND grant and uncovered amount without saying the government reimburses 90% of deficits to the end of 2025-26 with no commitment after that, attributed the Treasury's finding on lower-income households to the OBR, and said Gateshead would benefit from basic rate income tax while also saying nothing flows to councils
entries.fix: SEND logic stated, claims attributed and the income tax paragraph rewritten before the document went further

entries.product: Budget 2026 economic analysis, 3 to 4 page version, draft of 30 October 2026
entries.what: The draft said the documents do not say whether the mayor's 20% comes from the central or local share, when the OBR says the growth accrues to mayors rather than central government. It also said miles driven are not published locally, when road traffic data is published by local authority, and listed two exclusions from the Treasury's distributional analysis when the £100 payment is also outside it
entries.fix: Corrected in the version Nathaniel finalised on 30 October 2026
